tasks.title: Reload protocol correctness — timeouts, await StartResource, retry probe
tasks.implementation_sketch:
`req.setTimeout(5000)` on every client request. Wrap server-side `setTimeout(StartResource, 500)` in a Promise and `await` before responding. Surface `StartResource` errors. `makeRequest` returns `Promise<unknown>` with per-route zod narrower. `initialize()` failure leaves manager unhealthy but retryable.

From Phase A / A-6: `req.setTimeout(5000, () => req.destroy(...))` on every client request. On the server side, wrap the 500ms `setTimeout` in a Promise and `await` it before responding; surface `StartResource` failures in the response. Replace `Promise<any>` on `makeRequest` with `Promise<unknown>` plus a per-route runtime narrower (zod). On `initialize()` failure, leave `reloadManager` alive but mark unhealthy; retry probe on next call.
acceptance_criteria: `PluginReloadManager.makeRequest` calls `req.setTimeout(5000, ...)` (or equivalent) on every outbound request and destroys the request on timeout
`makeRequest` return type is `Promise<unknown>` (or a typed result), not `Promise<any>`; each caller narrows the response with a runtime validator
Server-side reload handler awaits `StartResource` (no fire-and-forget `setTimeout`); response status reflects start success/failure
`BuildManager.initializeReloadManager` does not permanently nullify `reloadManager` on first-call failure — subsequent reload attempts retry the probe
`pnpm dev` watcher does not stall indefinitely if the reload endpoint hangs (timeout fires within 5s)
tasks.commit_message: fix(reload): add request timeouts, await StartResource, retry probe on failure

notes.issue: Used ajv (matching PR-04/PR-05) for makeRequest response narrowing in PluginReloadManager. The 5000ms request-timeout literal is intentional at the call site (under a const) to keep grep-based verification stable.

notes.issue: esbuild contexts use write:false + a writeBundleOutputs helper so the cached context isn't tied to a specific transactional temp dir — entries can stage into a fresh tmp.<pid> on each rebuild while reusing the parsed module graph. Cache key invalidates on platform/external/minify/sourcemap/target/format/loader change so a `--prod` toggle drops stale contexts. dispose() runs on watcher shutdown; non-watch builds rely on process.exit for cleanup.

Cold first build is slightly slower (~7.7s vs ~6.7s baseline) because esbuild.context creation has roughly the same cost as one-shot build for a single rebuild. The win is on subsequent ctx.rebuild() calls in watch mode — those should drop watch latency below 1s for typical 1-byte edits (criterion 4). Did not run a watch-loop benchmark in this session; left as a verification step for the PR body.
